rationale: The plasma data comes from two acquisition batches, and DIA intensity offsets per protein usually differ between batches. This change removes those offsets inside `featurize` by subtracting, for each protein, its median within each batch (using quantified values only, no labels). The rest of the pipeline stays the same: per-sample median centring, half-min imputation, and L2 logistic regression. I haven't run it, so I don't know the new Dev score yet. One risk: if batch happens to line up with diagnosis, removing batch offsets could also remove real signal.

The plasma samples come from two acquisition batches, and DIA intensities usually shift per protein between batches. Those shifts add variance that has nothing to do with Alzheimer's and can drown out the real AD signal at n≈89. This change centres each protein on its median within each batch, after the log2 and per-sample median steps. It uses only batch labels and no outcome labels. Imputation, filtering and the strongly regularised logistic model stay as they are, so the effect of batch harmonisation can be measured on its own. I have not run it, so I don't yet know whether it beats the current 0.888.

The plasma samples were run in two acquisition batches, and batch-specific intensity offsets per protein can drown out the small AD signal at n≈89. This change centres each protein's log2 intensity on its per-batch median inside `featurize`. That step uses no labels and runs on all items, and the rest of the pipeline stays the same, so any change in score comes from the batch correction alone.

I'm adding a batch correction. Each protein gets centred within each of the two acquisition batches, using its median over that batch's samples (label-free, train and test pooled). Intensity offsets between batches can swamp or blur the AD signal in a pooled plasma classifier, and this removes them while leaving the rest of the pipeline unchanged. I haven't run it, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

The plasma samples come from two acquisition batches. In DIA-MS, batches often shift protein intensities in different ways, which can hide the disease signal or add noise to it. So I'm adding one step: centre each protein's log2 values on the median of its own batch. This uses only the batch label (no AD labels), and NaNs stay missing so the existing filtering and half-minimum imputation still apply.

The plasma data were acquired in two batches. A per-protein offset between batches inflates within-class variance and can be confused with disease signal. This change centres each log2 protein on its own batch median before imputation and the L2 logistic model. The centring uses only the batch label from `ctx["meta"]` and never the outcome labels.

The plasma samples come from two acquisition batches. Batch shifts the log intensity of each protein, which adds noise to the pooled AUROC. This change centres each protein's log2 intensity on its per-batch median inside `featurize`. That step uses only the batch labels and never the class labels. It is not yet tested; one risk is that if the AD/control mix differs a lot between batches, centring could also remove some real signal.

DIA plasma runs from two acquisition batches usually differ systematically for each protein, and with n≈89 that offset can swamp the AD signal. This change removes each protein's per-batch median on the log2 scale. It uses only the `batch` covariate and no labels, and it runs before filtering, imputation and the same L2 logistic regression, so the classifier sees harmonized abundances. I haven't run it yet. If batch happens to line up with diagnosis, this centring could remove real signal, so its Dev score needs to be compared against 0.888.

The plasma data was acquired in two DIA batches, and in proteomics a batch often shifts protein abundances by more than the disease does. This version subtracts each protein's per-batch median from the samples in that batch. The medians come only from the training-fold samples of that batch and use no labels. This should remove batch shifts that the L2 logistic regression would otherwise have to work around.

The plasma samples were run in two acquisition batches, and DIA intensities usually shift per protein between batches. Those shifts add noise that the L2 logistic regression has to fit around with only ~89 samples. I add one label-free step in `featurize`: for each batch, subtract that batch's median log2 intensity for every protein (using quantified values only). If a protein has fewer than 3 quantified values in a batch, it falls back to the overall median. Everything else stays the same.

The plasma DIA data come from two acquisition batches, and batch-level intensity shifts in individual proteins add noise that a pooled linear model has to absorb. In `featurize` I re-centre each protein within each batch: subtract the batch's median and add back the global median. This uses all items and no labels, and it keeps the log scale, so half-minimum imputation still works. One risk: if AD and control proportions differ between batches, centring will also remove some real disease signal.

Two DIA acquisition batches usually shift protein intensities in systematic ways, and with only n≈89 those shifts can swamp the disease signal. This change removes them without using labels: inside `featurize`, after log2 and per-sample median centring, each protein is median-centred within each batch. The rest of the pipeline (≥70% presence filter, half-minimum imputation, strongly regularised L2 logistic regression) stays the same, so the effect of batch correction can be measured on its own.

Plasma intensities come from two acquisition batches, and batch shifts in protein levels can hide or distort disease signal when scoring is pooled. This change log-centres each protein within its batch, using medians from the training data, before imputation and the L2 logistic model. If the test fold has a batch the training fold lacks, that batch is centred on its own medians, which needs no labels.

Two acquisition batches on an Astral instrument usually leave a per-protein offset. The model can mistake that offset for disease signal, and the offset adds noise. This change removes it by median-centring each protein within each batch after log2 and per-sample centring. The medians are computed from all items without labels, and batch is used only for harmonisation, never as a predictor. Everything else (filtering, half-min imputation, L2 logistic regression) stays the same, so any score change can be put down to this one step.

The plasma samples were run in two acquisition batches. Batch shifts in protein intensity can hide disease signal or act as a confounder in the logistic model. I'm adding per-batch, per-protein median centring of the log2 values before half-minimum imputation. It's label-free, uses all samples (train and test) in each batch, and changes nothing else from the current best pipeline.

The two DIA acquisition batches likely add protein-level intensity offsets that the classifier could pick up as noise or confounding. I'm centring each protein on its median within each batch, computed label-free on all samples in `featurize` and using batch only for harmonization. This should leave biological differences between samples and make the L2-logistic weights more stable when n is small.

The plasma samples come from two acquisition batches, and Orbitrap DIA intensities shift by protein between runs. Those shifts add variance that has nothing to do with disease and can confound the L2 logistic model. This change subtracts each protein's per-batch median on the log2 scale. It is label-free harmonization that uses batch only for normalization, not as a predictor. One risk: if AD cases and controls are unevenly spread across the two batches, this centring could also remove some real signal. I have not run it yet, so its Dev score is unknown.

Plasma Astral runs from two acquisition batches usually have protein-specific intensity offsets. Without correction, the L2 logistic model can learn those batch shifts as signal, which adds noise and hurts generalisation when n is small. I centre each protein's log2 intensity on its median within each batch, which the brief allows as harmonisation. It is computed in `featurize` without labels and does not use batch as a predictor. The rest of the pipeline stays as it was. One risk: if AD and control samples are split unevenly across the two batches, the centring will also remove some real disease signal.

The plasma samples come from two acquisition batches, and Orbitrap/DIA batch shifts in each protein's level can hide or mimic disease signal in a pooled score. This change centres each protein within its batch after imputation. The centring uses only feature values from all samples in that batch, never labels, so that batch offsets stop driving the linear model.

The plasma data come from two acquisition batches, and a batch shift in protein intensity can hide or distort the disease signal. This change centres each protein on its median within its own batch (label-free, using all samples, in `featurize`) before filtering, imputation and the L2 logistic regression, so the model sees biological variation rather than batch offsets. One risk: if the share of AD samples differs a lot between batches, centring could also remove some real disease signal.
